review.tagline: Python agent that carries out terminal-entered tasks with LLM tools and a browser
review.summary: OpenManus is a Python agent framework, an open reimplementation of Manus, that takes a task typed in the terminal and carries it out with tools. It drives a browser through the Browser Use CLI MCP server and calls an LLM endpoint configured in config.toml. Extra entry points cover an MCP tool version, an experimental multi-agent flow, and an optional data analysis agent.
review.audience: Developers wanting a hackable open Manus-style agent run from the terminal
strengths: Browser automation via Browser Use MCP server; local Chrome mode needs no API key
Separate entry points: main.py, run_mcp.py and run_flow.py for multi-agent
Simple config.toml with separate LLM and vision model settings
MIT license, active commits, and a Hugging Face demo space
weaknesses: Multi-agent flow is described by the README as unstable
Terminal-only interface, no web UI or user accounts
README shows only OpenAI-style API setup, no local model guidance
needs: Needs Python 3.12, uv or conda, LLM API key, Browser Use CLI (uvx), Chrome or Chromium, Playwright (BrowserGym)
Models: OpenAI-compatible API (gpt-4o in example config)
